title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (header '6-31', redaction n° 392) of the exercises to Commutative Algebra, Chap. VII ('Diviseurs'), §1. It sits between handwritten pages on L-functions of ℓ-adic sheaves, most likely because Grothendieck wrote his notes on the backs of Bourbaki drafts. The mathematics is P. Samuel's theory of purely inseparable descent of divisor class groups via logarithmic derivatives, in characteristic p = 2.

(End of Ex. 23) In an example ring, div_B(Z) is not the image of a divisor of A. Suppose the ramification index e(P/p) = 1 with P = BZ. Then A would contain a uniformizer of B_P of the form a(X,Y,Z)Z with b = a(X,Y,0) ≠ 0. This forces Δb/b = -XY, which is contradicted by computing Δ(-XY).

Ex. 24 a) Setting: L a field of characteristic 2, Δ a derivation, K = ker Δ, [L:K] = 2.
- Δ² is again a derivation (characteristic 2). It kills K and so is K-linear. Since Der_K(L) is one-dimensional over L, we get Δ² = aΔ, and one shows a ∈ K.
- The logarithmic derivatives t = Δx/x are exactly the t with Δt = at + t². This is the char-2 case of Jacobson's criterion Δ^{p-1}t + t^p = a t (with Δ^p = aΔ).

Ex. 24 b) Setting: B a local UFD, and x, y ∈ m such that Δx, Δy generate the ideal q = (Δ(B)). Claim: a logarithmic derivative lying in q is the logarithmic derivative of a unit of B. Method: write t = rΔx + sΔy and use a).

Ex. 25 Setting: B = k[[X,Y]] in characteristic 2, with Δ(X) = Y^{2j} and Δ(Y) = X^{2i}. Then
- A = ker Δ ∩ B = k[[X², Y², X^{2i+1} + Y^{2j+1}]].
- Δ² = 0, so the relevant group is {F ∈ B : ΔF = F²}. Modulo logarithmic derivatives of units, it computes C(A) (Samuel's isomorphism, Ex. 23 b).
- Give X weight 2j+1 and Y weight 2i+1, filter by weight, and compute the graded pieces for q ≥ 4ij using 24 b).
- Result: C(A) contains a k-vector space of dimension N(i,j) = #{(a,b) : 0 ≤ a < i, 0 ≤ b < j, (2j+1)a + (2i+1)b ≥ 2ij}.

Ex. 25 b)
- AX² is prime, so inverting X² does not change the class group: C(A[X^{-2}]) ≅ C(A).
- A' = A[X^{-2}] is Dedekind, since B' = B[X^{-2}] is principal and integral over A'.
- Hence one gets a Dedekind domain with infinite class group (for k infinite, and suitable i, j).
errors: Notational clash in 25 a): 'L' denotes both the fraction field of B and the additive group {F ∈ B : ΔF = F²}. The sentence 'les éléments de L sont les séries formelles F∈B telles que ΔF = F²' must refer to the latter group (with a = 0 because Δ² = 0 here). L' denotes the logarithmic derivatives of units.
In 25 b), 'infinite class group' needs k infinite (and N(i,j) ≥ 1); this is implicit in the draft.
Cross-references are left blank ('n°  , prop.  '), as is usual in a draft.

ideas.what: Logarithmic-derivative characterization in a degree-p purely inseparable extension given by a derivation: Δ^p = aΔ and t is a log derivative iff Δ^{p-1}t + t^p = at
ideas.modern_name: Jacobson's differential Galois correspondence / Samuel's logarithmic derivative criterion
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Algèbre commutative Ch. VII §1 exercises; Samuel, Lectures on UFDs (Tata 1964)

ideas.what: Computation of C(A) for A = ker Δ in k[[X,Y]] via weighted-homogeneous filtration; explicit dimension N(i,j)
ideas.modern_name: Samuel's method for divisor class groups of purely inseparable descents (Zariski-Samuel type examples)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki AC VII; Samuel, 'Classes de diviseurs et dérivées logarithmiques', Topology 1964

ideas.what: Dedekind domain with infinite class group obtained by localizing such an A
ideas.modern_name: Dedekind domains with infinite class group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Samuel / Bourbaki (later Claborn: every abelian group is a class group)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a Bourbaki typescript draft of published exercises (AC VII), essentially due to Samuel. It is unrelated to the surrounding L-function notes and was presumably reused as scrap paper. Nothing here is by Grothendieck or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Header '6 - 31 - ... n° 392' is a Bourbaki draft number, not part of Grothendieck's notes.
In 25 a) the group L/L' is what is meant (not the fraction field); the transcription is otherwise faithful.
'-XY' in characteristic 2 equals XY; the sign is as typed.
